message.content: {"predictors": [{"name": "Short-Term Operating Leverage", "construction": "Change in operating income divided by change in sales over the past year (using quarterly Compustat data), averaged over the last four quarters.", "rationale": "Firms with higher operating leverage may be more sensitive to economic shocks, and investors might underappreciate this risk, leading to mispricing.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"}, {"name": "Inventory Growth Minus Sales Growth", "construction": "Annual percentage change in inventories minus annual percentage change in sales, both from Compustat.", "rationale": "Firms accumulating inventory faster than sales may be overproducing, indicating potential future problems that are not yet priced in.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure"}, {"name": "Recent Insider Buying Ratio", "construction": "Total shares purchased by insiders over the past six months divided by total shares outstanding (using SEC Form 4 filings and CRSP share counts).", "rationale": "Insider purchases may signal undervaluation or positive private information, which the market may not fully incorporate immediately.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"}, {"name": "R&D-to-Free-Cash-Flow Ratio", "construction": "Research and development expense divided by free cash flow (operating cash flow minus capital expenditures), both from Compustat, over the prior fiscal year.", "rationale": "Firms investing heavily in R&D relative to cash flows may be positioned for future growth undervalued by the market.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"}, {"name": "Post-Earnings Drift Magnitude", "construction": "Cumulative abnormal return in the 60 days following the most recent quarterly earnings announcement (using CRSP and quarterly earnings dates).", "rationale": "Market underreaction to earnings surprises can persist; stocks with high post-earnings drift may continue to outperform.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"}, {"name": "Dividend Change Surprise", "construction": "Actual dividend change minus the average of analyst forecasted dividend changes (using IBES forecasts and CRSP/Compustat dividend data), standardized by market capitalization.", "rationale": "Positive dividend surprises may signal management confidence, leading to upward price momentum.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"}, {"name": "Accounts Receivable Turnover Change", "construction": "Current year accounts receivable turnover (sales divided by average accounts receivable) minus prior year value, from Compustat.", "rationale": "Improving collections efficiency may indicate strengthening fundamentals not yet reflected in prices.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"}, {"name": "Share Repurchase Intensity", "construction": "Dollar value of shares repurchased over the past year divided by market capitalization, using Compustat and CRSP.", "rationale": "Repurchases can signal undervaluation and reduce agency costs, potentially leading to higher future performance.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"}, {"name": "Segment Diversification Discount", "construction": "Difference between a firm’s market-to-book ratio and the value-weighted market-to-book ratios of its individual segments (using Compustat segment data).", "rationale": "Conglomerate firms with larger diversification discounts may be undervalued relative to their parts.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure"}, {"name": "Tax Loss Carryforward Ratio", "construction": "Total tax loss carryforwards divided by total assets, from Compustat annual data.", "rationale": "Firms with large carryforwards may have valuable tax shields underappreciated by investors.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"}]}
